title: Vendor onboarding: privileged keys, pricing readout & DPA clarifications
summary: Initial procurement + security alignment for vendor onboarding. Discussed DPA exceptions, KMS/HSM options for privileged keys, SSO/SAML, pricing scenarios (committed vs pay-as-you-go), and a short technical preflight for private connectivity. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send pricing scenarios and security pack; customer to share data residency appendix and schedule a network runbook session with infra team.
action_items: Maya Patel - send two pricing scenarios (committed monthly reserved vs hosted pay-as-you-go) plus sample quote spreadsheet by 2025-10-24
Evan Cole - prepare short tech runbook for KMS integration and private VPC egress checklist by 2025-10-27
Lena Ortiz - circulate Cobalt data residency appendix and list of compliance stakeholders by 2025-10-23
Ravi Singh - schedule a 1-hour network connectivity call with Cobalt infra and Redwood SEs week of 2025-10-27
next_steps: Redwood to share security package (SOC2 report, DPA redline template, KMS integration notes)
Customer to confirm preferred pricing path and internal approvers
Schedule technical runbook / network preflight with infra team
Follow-up pricing readout meeting (if needed) in one week
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: 49m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Cole (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Cobalt Head Procurement), Ravi Singh (Cobalt Security Architect), Tom Weller (Cobalt Finance)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick intro - I'm Maya, the AE on this deal, and Evan is our solutions engineer. We'll run through the legal and procurement items, and then Evan will cover the tech bits for keys and connectivity.
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: Hi Maya, hi Evan. From procurement side we'll want to walk the DPA and pricing. Tom is here from finance and Ravi will handle security questions.
[00:30] Tom Weller: Yep, hi all. We're looking to close budgeting by end of month which is tight.
[00:42] Evan Cole: Great, I'll try to keep the technical part short. Just to set expectations: Redwood can support hosted API, reserved dedicated capacity and private deployment. For privileged keys we support customer-managed KMS integrations and in some deployments HSM-backed keying.
[00:58] Ravi Singh: When you say HSM-backed, are you supporting customer HSMs behind a VPC or is it Redwood-managed HSM? That makes a difference for our compliance review.
[01:12] Evan Cole: We support both patterns. For Redwood Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS via cross-account roles and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flows. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed KMS; HSM access is available via dedicated private deployments where keys never leave your control. Sorry, little word salad there.
[01:30] Lena Ortiz: That's helpful. On the DPA side our legal team flagged two items: data residency appendix and audit log retention. We need confirmation on where logs live and whether log exports are possible into our S3.
[01:44] Maya Patel: Yes, audit logs can be exported. For dedicated and private deployments logs remain in your tenancy and we can arrange exports to your S3 or SIEM. For hosted there's an export pipeline and we can push to S3 with a contractual SLA, we should flag the export latency though.
[02:02] Ravi Singh: And SOC 2? We need SOC 2 Type II and evidence.
[02:08] Maya Patel: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II; we'll include the attestation in the security pack.
[02:14] Tom Weller: Pricing — we are sensitive to egress and per-token cost. What's the tradeoff between reserved dedicated capacity and hosted?
[02:26] Maya Patel: Good question. Reserved gives lower unit costs and predictable throughput, but requires monthly commit. Hosted is pay-as-you-go, higher per-token cost but no commit and quicker time to value. We'll send a side-by-side scenario spreadsheet.
[02:40] Tom Weller: Can you give ballpark numbers now?
[02:44] Maya Patel: Ballpark: hosted X cents per 1k tokens, reserved can drop that by 30-50% depending on commitment size. I'll avoid precise numbers in call because the spreadsheet will show tiers and committed discounts.
[02:58] Lena Ortiz: Also need clarity on data retention for prompts and generated outputs — do you retain customer data for training?
[03:06] Evan Cole: Redwood does not use customer data to train models in hosted or dedicated with the standard DPA; we have an opt-in telemetry bucket for quality that is off by default. For private deployments you control data entirely.
[03:20] Ravi Singh: Good. On the KMS integration detail, what network path does the KMS use? Does Redwood make outbound connections to our KMS endpoint, or do we have to push certificates?
[03:32] Evan Cole: For cross-account KMS we use a secured outbound call from the inference nodes to your KMS endpoint over private network peering (VPC peering / AWS PrivateLink). We also support customer side certificate rotation and periodic re-keying. We'll send a short runbook that covers ports, IP ranges, and required firewall rules.
[03:50] Lena Ortiz: Great, include that runbook please.
[03:54] [04:00] Maya Patel: Quick procurement note — the DPA we typically sign has a data residency appendix that we can either accept your template or propose our standard. If you have an internal DPA redline we can review.
[04:12] Lena Ortiz: We do have an appendix with EU-only residency. That will determine whether we do hosted in our region or need dedicated.
[04:20] Ravi Singh: EU residency plus HSM means private deployment probably, right?
[04:24] Evan Cole: Often yes, because with private you can keep keys and logs within the EU tenancy. But sometimes customers use dedicated regional pods; it's a tradeoff between operational overhead and unit cost.
[04:36] Tom Weller: Timeline question — we're budgeting this quarter; can you commit to onboarding in November if procurement signs off?
[04:44] Maya Patel: If procurement and legal clear within the next two weeks, we can schedule onboarding in early November. We'll need a short network preflight and a pilot window.
[04:54] Lena Ortiz: Sounds tight but possible.
[04:56] [05:00] Evan Cole: On the technical POC: we propose a 2-week pilot with constrained throughput to validate latency and cost. During the pilot we'll enable prefix caching and batching suggestions to mirror your traffic patterns. Note, KV cache may be transcribed as K-V cash in some docs — just kidding — but we'll provide expected token distribution metrics.
[05:20] Ravi Singh: Can we run a 1k qps stress test?
[05:24] Evan Cole: For the pilot we typically run lower to validate correctness; for scale tests we do a separate benchmark window. If you want a 1k qps spike we can schedule that as a performance test with Redwood Dedicated or a temporary burst pool.
[05:40] Tom Weller: On billing — do you offer invoice terms 30 vs 60?
[05:44] Maya Patel: We can accommodate Net 30 standard. For enterprise reserved we'd discuss invoice terms as part of commercial negotiations.
[05:54] Lena Ortiz: A few legal redlines: limitation of liability cap, security indemnities, and data deletion timeline. We may propose 30 days post-termination for deletion and certification.
[06:06] Maya Patel: Noted. Our standard DPA includes 30-day deletion and certification, though enterprise customers sometimes ask for compressed windows; we'll note that for legal.
[06:16] [06:30] Maya Patel: Okay Evan, can you run through the KMS integration examples and what artifacts you will send?
[06:36] Evan Cole: Sure. We'll send: (1) KMS integration runbook with endpoints and firewall rules; (2) key rotation and access pattern doc; (3) sample IAM cross-account policy for AWS KMS; (4) diagram showing network flows for private deployment vs hosted. Also a short checklist for certificate pinning if you use on-prem HSMs.
[06:58] Ravi Singh: For cross-account IAM policy — we need least privilege. Can we see the exact policy?
[07:04] Evan Cole: Yes, we'll include a least-privilege policy example in the runbook.
[07:08] Lena Ortiz: On the DPA redline: who will own the first pass?
[07:12] Maya Patel: Redwood can take first pass and include the standard security appendices; happy to take your redlines after. We'll put the redline link into the CRM.
[07:20] Tom Weller: What about SSO — SAML or OIDC?
[07:24] Maya Patel: We support SAML SSO for the console and API keys are scoped with RBAC. For enterprise we can do SCIM for provisioning.
[07:34] Ravi Singh: RBAC — are token scopes auditable? We need audit trails showing who called which route.
[07:42] Evan Cole: Yes, audit logs include token-level traces and route-level latency/cost breakdown. For dedicated and private you control log retention and export; hosted we maintain logs but can export per contract.
[07:56] Lena Ortiz: Can you include a sample SLA for latency and uptime? Our ops team needs guaranteed SLOs.
[08:02] Maya Patel: We'll include a sample SLA doc. For dedicated we offer SLA-backed targets; hosted has best-effort plus analytics. We'll call out failover and automatic fallback policies in that doc.
[08:16] [08:30] Tom Weller: About pricing again — hidden egress fees for log exports?
[08:34] Maya Patel: Egress to your S3 in the same region is typically no additional charge; cross-region or third-party transfer might incur network fees. We'll note these explicitly in the spreadsheet.
[08:46] Lena Ortiz: Good. Also need a clear onboarding runbook: legal -> procurement -> infra -> pilot -> prod.
[08:54] Maya Patel: We'll propose an onboarding cadence in the follow-up email.
[08:58] Evan Cole: One more technical caveat: quantization and model variant selection affects throughput and quality. If you have large context lengths we recommend specific model profiles. We'll include suggestions in the Optimize playbook.
[09:14] Ravi Singh: Do you support bringing our own models in private deployment?
[09:18] Evan Cole: In private deployments yes — you can deploy customers' models, but there's an on-boarding vetting and licensing review. We'll add the process doc.
[09:28] Lena Ortiz: Okay, from procurement side next steps would be the pricing scenarios and a redline DPA. We'll queue legal's internal review.

[09:40] Maya Patel: To recap: Redwood will send pricing scenarios, security pack (SOC2 attestation, DPA template), KMS runbook, and sample SLA. Cobalt will send the data residency appendix and schedule a network preflight with their infra team.
[09:58] Ravi Singh: I'll coordinate times with Evan for the network call.
[10:02] Tom Weller: Finance will triage the quote once we get the tiered spreadsheet.
[10:10] Lena Ortiz: We'll aim for internal approvals by 2025-10-30.
[10:14] Maya Patel: Perfect — action items captured. Anything else before we close?
[10:20] Ravi Singh: One tiny ask — can you also include a short note on incident response and contact points?
[10:26] Maya Patel: Absolutely, we'll add the incident response contact and on-call process in the security pack.
[10:34] Evan Cole: I'll drop the runbook and a short diagram into the follow-up.
[10:40] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Thursday.
[10:44] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, bye.

[End of transcript]
